name: tailcat
description: like netcat, but over Tailscale's data plane, without Tailscale's control plane
one_liner: A stripped-down networking tool for sysadmins that sets up an encrypted point-to-point connection between two machines, borrowing Tailscale's tunneling tech without needing a Tailscale account.
buyer: Honestly, nobody buys this directly — it's a free command-line utility for network engineers and sysadmins doing one-off debugging, not something with a paying customer.
business_use_cases: A sysadmin uses it for a quick ad hoc encrypted file transfer between two servers without setting up a full Tailscale network.
A security researcher uses it to test NAT traversal and relay behavior while experimenting with WireGuard-based tunnels.
A systems integrator might mention it as a component in a larger bespoke networking project, but it isn't itself a product.

money_ideas.idea: No standalone revenue model — it's a developer utility, not a product; any money is made building something bigger around it

steal_this: There's no weekend business here. It's a well-made plumbing tool, not a product — skip it unless you're building infrastructure that needs exactly this primitive.
